title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01); with n = 1 and n10 = 1 the archived two-sided p = 1.00 under that convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks such as translation of operator intent to device configuration, multi-step change planning, and programmatic repairs. System reports and surveys emphasize that operational safety depends heavily on surrounding engineering: deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A widely proposed operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM generates a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks a set of formalized properties, and automated or human-in-the-loop repairs are applied for violations.

Despite conceptual consensus, controlled measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a verifier (holding the model’s proposal fixed) are scarce. Practitioners need to know: when an LLM already produces high-quality candidates, how much incremental safety does a verifier plus a modest automated repair budget provide on a verifier-scoped pass/fail metric? We address this narrowly and operationally: given identical initial proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how much does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM alone? We preregistered a paired confirmatory design, executed it under a hosted adapter, and archive all artifacts for deterministic re-inspection.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic/formal verification tools and techniques (header-space analyses, route-model verifiers, Batfish-style checkers) provide machine-checkable properties such as reachability/isolation and update atomicity and are well-established in NetOps verification literature [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps research demonstrates LLM integration for intent parsing and configuration generation while strongly advocating operational guardrails (INTA, Confucius, and other agentic NetOps frameworks) [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair patterns are broadly proposed across structured-generation domains to reduce unsafe or incorrect outputs [PoeTone; INTA].

Separate literature documents systemic LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommends verification or human oversight as mitigations [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. What is missing is a controlled, preregistered ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms. Our study produces such an artifact-backed measurement and situates it relative to these prior works.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and plan. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026, freezing research questions, inclusion/exclusion rules, task-generator seeds, estimands, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to execution. Primary hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration, seeds, and artifacts are archived (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Task corpus and stratification. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was generated with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 using preregistered seeds and deterministic replacement rules. Tasks were stratified across three intent-change clusters: VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change. The preregistered allocation was 167/167/166 respectively; the archived execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation report no deviations from the preregistered sampling plan (deviations_from_preregistration = []). Therefore the realized per-cluster composition in the executed confirmatory set matches the preregistered allocation: VLAN-change = 167, ACL-change = 167, static-route-change = 166. Task inputs were constrained to the verifier-modeled features (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}) so that the deterministic validator could score each proposal against preregistered property coverage.

Generation semantics and isolation. To isolate verifier+repair impact we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false). For each task a single shared LLM proposal was recorded; that identical proposal served as the baseline outcome and was also fed to the guarded arm. The guarded arm invoked the automated single-repair call only when the deterministic verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. This choice prevents conflation with verifier-guided regeneration and isolates the effect of verification plus at most one repair applied to the same initial proposal.

Models, adapter, and verifier. The requested LLM was gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses). Model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) specified max_output_tokens = 2000 and single-attempt generation. The gating and scoring verifier was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; its validator-spec and the mapping of violation codes to severity levels are archived in the execution bundle. The guarded arm allowed up to one automated repair invocation per preregistration.

Confirmatory inference and implementation detail. The preregistered confirmatory test is McNemar’s paired test on task-level binary outcomes. Our archived analysis executor implements the standard exact approach that reduces to an exact binomial test on the number of discordant pairs: let n = n10 + n01 be the discordant-pair count and let k = n10 be the count of pairs where guarded passes and baseline fails (discordant in the direction of improvement). Under the null H0 (no directional effect) X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5). The two-sided p-value reported by the archived executor is p_two-sided = 2·min{P(X ≤ k), P(X ≥ k)} with a cap of 1.0 to handle small-n symmetry. This exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs implementation and the code-path used are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We report the executor’s archived two-sided p-value (p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts) and complement it with a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) for the absolute difference.
sections.results:
Run and accounting summary. Execution completed under the preregistered stopping rule with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500, repair-stage calls = 1); failed_episode_count = 0. Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). Paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact test and CI. Using the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, k = 1). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). These analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and reproduce the reported statistics deterministically.

Repair provenance and the discordant episode. Observed repair-stage calls = 1 and that single automated repair produced the lone discordant outcome (n10 = 1): the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verifier pass. The archived per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, and repair-provider traces record this episode. For auditability we include the deterministic retrieval method and a succinct artifact-backed summary here: the unique discordant episode is recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl as the single pair for which the baseline scoring field indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation while the guarded scoring field indicates pass. The execution-level manifests (execution_manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirm exactly one repair-stage call and one such discordant pair. The guarded repair cleared the verifier-scoped violation according to the verifier’s post-repair validation (the archived validator_trace marks the final configuration as valid and records repair_applied and the repair prompt/response). Because the raw_results.jsonl and provider-call traces are archived in the evidence bundle, auditors can deterministically locate the exact pair and inspect the full validator and repair traces.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime — single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration — the LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This demonstrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is extremely high for the verifier-modeled properties, a modest verify→repair budget may yield negligible measured pass-rate gains on a composite pass/fail metric, while still being able to correct rare concrete failures.

Design-choice implications. Our shared-initial semantics intentionally answer the operational question of marginal verifier benefit when deployments prefer to preserve the original proposal (e.g., for human review) and apply repairs rather than regenerate. This design choice reduces model-call overhead (observed model_calls_used = 501) but omits potential gains available with verifier-guided regeneration or multiple repair iterations; those alternatives require separate preregistrations and measurement because they change both the intervention and the resource accounting.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: preregistration, deterministic seeds, and automated replacement rules protected against design drift; no confirmatory exclusions or provider failures occurred. Construct validity: the pass==no-high/medium-severity-violation outcome is defined relative to the deterministic validator’s modeled coverage and severity mapping archived in the validator-spec; properties outside the modeled scope were intentionally excluded by task construction. External validity: results are conditional on a single model family, a synthetic task corpus constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}, and a single verifier implementation — we do not claim multi-model or cross-vendor generality.

Statistical nuance. The archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 is a direct consequence of the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs implementation and the observed tiny discordant-n (n = 1). Small-n exact two-sided p-values can appear counterintuitive; the paired-bootstrap CI provides a complementary uncertainty measure. Together they show that while the point estimate improvement exists (0.002), inference is limited by ceiling effects and few discordant outcomes.

Operational recommendations. (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative operational data before committing repair budget: extremely low baseline error prevalence reduces marginal pass-rate returns. (2) Align verifier coverage with operator-critical constraints; expand verifier modeling where important production properties are outside the current coverage. (3) Choose generation semantics consistent with deployment priorities: shared-initial saves model-call budget and preserves original proposals for review, whereas regeneration-based guarded workflows may increase final-pass probability at a higher model-call cost.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N = 500) isolating the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for verifier-modeled properties and verifier coverage is limited, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget may be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, though the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures. We recommend practitioners measure baseline error prevalence on representative workloads, align verifier coverage with operator priorities, and select generation/repair semantics to match deployment constraints. All preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every claim made here.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic task corpus constrained to features modeled by the deterministic validator (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}); results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; iterative or regeneration-based strategies might change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicates pass == 1; because exactly one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup deterministically returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
